title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #12

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word cup? (1 mark)
   A. cup's
   B. cupes
   C. cuppies
   D. cups

2. How should you find out how your mother tongue forms plurals? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   B. Ignore it
   C. Add s to every word
   D. Guess from English

3. A noun is a word that (1 mark)
   A. joins two sentences
   B. describes a colour only
   C. names a person, animal, place or thing
   D. shows an action

4. Which of these is NOT a way of building vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping a word bank
   B. Using a dictionary
   C. Making flashcards
   D. Never looking at new words

5. In Simon says, when should you obey an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Only if you like it
   B. Only when it begins with Simon says
   C. Always
   D. Never

6. Which words show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. first, then, next
   B. mother, father
   C. red, blue, green
   D. sun, rain

7. Which is a verb in: The pot tipped over? (1 mark)
   A. pot
   B. over
   C. The
   D. tipped

8. Which of these is a safety rule from the road safety dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Run across without looking
   B. Play on the road
   C. Look right, then left, then right again
   D. Cross anywhere

9. Which sentence belongs to the main idea Fire is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. The market is far.
   B. Maize is tasty.
   C. Never play with matches.
   D. Rain is wet.

10. Which words signal a simile? (1 mark)
   A. like and as
   B. but and or
   C. to and from
   D. is and are

11. In the metaphor Time is money, what is the meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Time is made of paper
   B. Clocks are coins
   C. Money is a clock
   D. Time is valuable and should not be wasted

12. In The farmer was weary after a long day in the shamba, weary means (1 mark)
   A. very hungry
   B. very loud
   C. very rich
   D. very tired

13. What does Asiyesikia la mkuu huvunjika guu teach? (1 mark)
   A. Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   B. Elders are always wrong
   C. Never walk
   D. Legs are weak

14. What does a peer review checklist help with? (1 mark)
   A. Checking a partner's story kindly
   B. Cleaning the room
   C. Ending the lesson
   D. Stealing ideas

15. What is the language train game? (1 mark)
   A. A game with real trains
   B. A running race
   C. A reading test
   D. Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when

16. Which question helps you plan an experience to tell? (1 mark)
   A. What colour is the wall?
   B. Who was there?
   C. Where is the moon?
   D. How long is the ruler?

17. Which comma use is correct? (1 mark)
   A. When, the bell rang we ran.
   B. When the bell, rang we ran.
   C. When the bell rang we, ran.
   D. When the bell rang, we ran.

18. What is skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Reading backwards
   B. Reading slowly for every word
   C. Copying the text
   D. Reading quickly to get the main idea

19. What should you keep in mind when scanning? (1 mark)
   A. What you are looking for
   B. Nothing
   C. A song
   D. A poem

20. Which strategy would you use to find a price in an advert? (1 mark)
   A. Scanning
   B. Skimming
   C. Drawing
   D. Singing

21. Which word shows a result? (1 mark)
   A. but
   B. and
   C. or
   D. so

22. What is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A sentence with one word
   B. A title
   C. Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   D. A list

23. What does a preposition show? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of a thing
   B. The price of goods
   C. The position of one thing in relation to another
   D. The sound of an animal

24. The bag is below the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. beside
   B. between
   C. on
   D. under

25. What is a group of lines in a poem called? (1 mark)
   A. A sentence
   B. A stanza
   C. A paragraph
   D. A chapter

26. How should peer feedback be given? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Loudly
   C. Rudely
   D. Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion

27. What are the events of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The author
   B. What happens step by step
   C. The margin
   D. The title

28. What should you do first when studying a picture for a story? (1 mark)
   A. Copy a story
   B. Look at the whole picture
   C. Cover it
   D. Write the ending

29. What is a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A song
   C. A game of football
   D. A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons

30. What are notes? (1 mark)
   A. Songs
   B. Long stories
   C. Pictures only
   D. Short records of important points

31. What is the main idea of a passage? (1 mark)
   A. The page number
   B. What it is mostly about
   C. The date
   D. The last word

32. What is a stage direction? (1 mark)
   A. The ending
   B. An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   C. A price
   D. The title

33. What is a call centre? (1 mark)
   A. A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   B. A farm
   C. A market
   D. A school

34. Which is a part of a form? (1 mark)
   A. Title
   B. Riddle
   C. Ending song
   D. Poem

35. What does a signature show? (1 mark)
   A. Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   B. The price of a form
   C. The colour of a pen
   D. The paper size

36. What should you do when someone else is speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Listen without interrupting
   B. Draw
   C. Leave
   D. Talk over them

37. What is a stanza? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. A single word
   C. A group of lines in a poem
   D. A rhyme only

38. What is a line in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. One row of words
   B. A whole page
   C. A book
   D. A stanza

39. Why should instruction charts use large clear letters? (1 mark)
   A. So people can read them from a distance
   B. To make them heavy
   C. To use more ink
   D. To hide meaning

40. What should each step in written instructions usually start with? (1 mark)
   A. A number only
   B. A colour
   C. A name
   D. A verb

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. List three polite expressions used during a telephone call. (3 marks)

42. Give three tips for telling a story well. (3 marks)

43. Give three rules of good telephone manners. (3 marks)

44. List the two verbs in the sentence: The teacher counted the votes and announced the winner. (2 marks)

45. List three habits of an attentive listener. (3 marks)

46. Give three questions to ask when reading an advert. (3 marks)

47. Name two elements of a story. (2 marks)

48. Put in order: shillings the pays customer fifty (3 marks)

49. Name two digital devices and give a use of each. (2 marks)

50. Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them. (3 marks)

51. Name four question words used to check comprehension. (2 marks)

52. Explain what a form is. (2 marks)

53. Explain why clear instructions are important on a road. (3 marks)

54. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

55. Give three signal words used to show the order of steps. (3 marks)

56. Compose a four-line poem about leisure that includes two interjections. (5 marks)

57. Explain when you would skim and when you would scan. Give one example of each. (5 marks)

58. Join with but: The trader was tired. He kept working. (3 marks)

59. List the verbs in: Otieno touched the handle and the water splashed. (3 marks)

60. List the six elements of a story. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — cups
   Most English nouns add s to make the plural.

2. A — Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   Languages form plurals in different ways, so we ask people who know the language well.

3. C — names a person, animal, place or thing
   Nouns are naming words.

4. D — Never looking at new words
   Ignoring new words does not build vocabulary.

5. B — Only when it begins with Simon says
   The game is about listening carefully.

6. A — first, then, next
   Sequence words show the order.

7. D — tipped
   Tipped shows what the pot did.

8. C — Look right, then left, then right again
   The dialogue teaches how to look before crossing.

9. C — Never play with matches.
   It is a detail about fire safety.

10. A — like and as
   Similes use like or as.

11. D — Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   The metaphor shows the value of time.

12. D — very tired
   A long day of work suggests tiredness.

13. A — Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   It means one who does not listen to the elders may come to harm.

14. A — Checking a partner's story kindly
   Peer review helps improve writing.

15. D — Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   Each pupil adds a when sentence.

16. B — Who was there?
   Who, what, where, when, why and how help plan a story.

17. D — When the bell rang, we ran.
   A comma follows the when part at the start.

18. D — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the general idea.

19. A — What you are looking for
   Scanning needs a target.

20. A — Scanning
   You know exactly what you need.

21. D — so
   So shows a result.

22. C — Two simple sentences joined by a conjunction
   It joins two ideas.

23. C — The position of one thing in relation to another
   Prepositions show position such as on, under and beside.

24. D — under
   Under means below something.

25. B — A stanza
   A stanza is a group of lines.

26. D — Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   Kind feedback helps writers.

27. B — What happens step by step
   Events are the actions in order.

28. B — Look at the whole picture
   First see the whole picture.

29. D — A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   A debate is an organised argument of a motion.

30. D — Short records of important points
   Notes are brief points.

31. B — What it is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

32. B — An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   Stage directions tell how to speak or move.

33. A — A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   Call centre staff answer calls.

34. A — Title
   A form has a title.

35. A — Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   A signature confirms you agree.

36. A — Listen without interrupting
   Respectful listening is key.

37. C — A group of lines in a poem
   A stanza is a group of lines.

38. A — One row of words
   Poems are written in lines.

39. A — So people can read them from a distance
   Clarity helps readers.

40. D — A verb
   Steps begin with action words.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Good morning, please, thank you, excuse me, goodbye, may I speak to (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Start with a clear opening, tell events in order, speak clearly, look at the audience, end with what you learned.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet, give your name, speak clearly, do not interrupt, do not call late without a reason, say goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: counted, announced
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb. Teacher, votes and winner are nouns.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Face the speaker, stay quiet, think about the words, wait for your turn, respond correctly (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each habit, up to three.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: What is being sold, who is it for, what is the price, where can I get it, is it as good as it says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: The customer pays fifty shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the words in order, one for the capital and one for the full stop.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Phone for calling, radio for hearing news, camera for taking photos (any two with uses).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each device with its use.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who, what, where, when, why, how (any four).
   Working / marking points: One mark for two correct question words and two marks for four.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form is a page with spaces where people write information in an organised way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a page with spaces and one for collecting information.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear road instructions and signs tell drivers and walkers what to do, which prevents accidents and keeps everyone safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for telling what to do, one for preventing accidents, one for safety.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines about free time with two suitable interjections, for example Wow, it is time to play! Hurray, no lessons today! We run and read and sing, Free time is a lovely thing.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each line up to four and one mark for two suitable interjections.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Skim when you want the main idea, for example looking through an article. Scan when you want one fact, for example looking for a name on a list.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two situations and two marks for examples and one mark for correct meaning.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: The trader was tired, but he kept working.
   Working / marking points: One mark for but, one for the comma, one for correct order.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: touched, splashed
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb and one mark for ignoring the nouns.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending.
   Working / marking points: Award 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, and 1 mark for two or three.
